newsitem.title: ITALY: Stet - golden share won't hit market value.
newsitem.headline: Stet - golden share won't hit market value.

text.p: Guido Rossi, chairman of Italy's state controlled telecoms holding Stet, said the introduction of a golden share did not reduce the market value of the group.
"I'm very sceptical about the golden share reducing the market value. In fact, since the announcement of the move the share price has risen," he told a parliamentary commission.

Stet shareholders last week approved the introduction of a golden share to be held by the Treasury in the future privatised group, giving the state special voting rights after it loses majority control for up to three years after the sell-off.
The Stet sale will take place this autumn after the holding is merged with its fixed-line telephone operator Telecom Italia.
At 1105 GMT, Stet shares were 1.15 percent up at 7,320 lire.
